stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
A rational map X⇢Y is an equivalence class of maps on dense opens of X; two representatives agree on some dense open inside their intersection. Birationality uses inverse rational maps.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume $X$ is reduced and $Y$ is separated over $S$. Let
$\varphi$ be a rational map from $X$ to $Y$ with domain of definition
$U \subset X$. Then there exists a unique morphism $f : U \to Y$
of algebraic spaces representing $\varphi$.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume $X$ is reduced and $Y$ is separated over $S$. Let
$\varphi$ be a rational map from $X$ to $Y$ with domain of definition
$U \subset X$.
conclusions:
there exists a unique morphism $f : U \to Y$
of algebraic spaces representing $\varphi$.

reason: Two representatives of the rational map agree on a dense open of their intersection. Separatedness of Y makes their equalizer closed; reducedness of X makes a closed subscheme containing a dense open equal to the whole intersection, so representatives glue uniquely over the full domain of definition.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
A rational map X⇢Y is an equivalence class of maps on dense opens of X; two representatives agree on some dense open inside their intersection. Birationality uses inverse rational maps.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic
space over $S$ with $|X|$ and $|Y|$ irreducible.
Then $X$ and $Y$ are birational if and only if
there are nonempty open subspaces $U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$
which are isomorphic as algebraic spaces over $S$.
hypotheses:
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ and $Y$ be algebraic
space over $S$ with $|X|$ and $|Y|$ irreducible.
conclusions:
$X$ and $Y$ are birational if and only if
there are nonempty open subspaces $U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$
which are isomorphic as algebraic spaces over $S$.

reason: Inverse dominant rational maps may be shrunk to morphisms whose compositions equal the identities on dense opens. Taking suitable inverse-image open subspaces in the respective irreducible spaces gives mutually inverse morphisms, hence isomorphic nonempty open subspaces; the converse is immediate.
